title: The state of ICT in Mozambique - Research ICT Africa

facts.fact: Mozambique's telecommunications market is structured around four vertically-integrated operators, including fixed-line incumbent TDM.
facts.quote: The telecommunications market is structured around four vertically-integrated operators, including fixed-line incumbent

facts.fact: According to the 2017 After Access Survey across 16 countries in the Global South, Mozambique's mobile phone penetration was 30%.
facts.quote: Mozambique had among the lowest mobile phone and Internet penetration rates, 30% and 10%, respectively.

facts.fact: Movitel's share of total mobile revenue rose to 27 percent in 2016, while mCel held 21 percent, according to the report.
facts.quote: subsequently increasing its revenue share to 27 percent in 2016, leaving mCel with only 21 percent of the total mobile revenue.

facts.fact: Movitel gained about 11 percent of mobile revenue share in 2012 before rising to 27 percent in 2016.
facts.quote: gaining about 11 percent in 2012 and subsequently increasing its revenue share to 27 percent in 2016

facts.fact: Vodacom Mozambique's data revenue grew by 31 percent, and its data customers increased by 63.6 percent.
facts.quote: Vodacom’s data revenue grew by 31 percent and data customers increased by 63.6 percent

facts.fact: Mobile phone adoption in Mozambique is 50 percent, the lowest among the surveyed countries.
facts.quote: Mozambique has the lowest mobile phone adoption level (50%)

facts.fact: The gender disparity in mobile phone ownership in Mozambique is 36 percent, the second highest after Rwanda's 38 percent.
facts.quote: the second highest gender disparity at 36 percent after Rwanda’s 38 percent

facts.fact: Half of men (50%) in Mozambique have mobile phones, compared with 32 percent of women.
facts.quote: More than half of all men (50%) have mobile phones as compared to only 32 percent of women.

facts.fact: Of Mozambicans who are offline (90%), 76 percent say they do not have devices to access the Internet.
facts.quote: Of those who are offline (90%), 76 percent stated that they do not have devices to access the Internet

facts.fact: Of Mozambicans who are offline, 14 percent say they do not know how to use the Internet.
facts.quote: while 14 percent stated they do not know how to use the Internet

facts.fact: 78 percent of respondents without a mobile phone say they cannot afford one.
facts.quote: 78 percent of the respondents stated that they cannot afford a mobile phone

facts.fact: 36 percent of those without mobile phones cite lack of electricity as the main reason.
facts.quote: A substantial proportion (36%) of those who do not have mobile phones reported lack of electricity as the main reason

facts.fact: Smartphone penetration in Mozambique is seven percent.
facts.quote: Mozambique stands at seven percent, which explains the low ten percent, Internet penetration in Mozambique.

facts.fact: About two-thirds (64%) of respondents without smartphones say smartphones are too expensive.
facts.quote: about two-thirds (64%) stated that smartphones are too expensive

facts.fact: Half of the Mozambican population has no access to electricity, compared with 6 percent in South Africa and 33 percent in Nigeria.
facts.quote: Half of the Mozambican population has no access to electricity, compared to only six percent in South Africa and 33 percent in Nigeria.

facts.fact: Mozambican authorities passed legislation in 2004 allowing mobile operators to partner with financial institutions to provide mobile money services.
facts.quote: Mozambican authorities passed legislation in 2004 allowing mobile operators to partner with financial institution

facts.fact: As of 2016, there were about three million mobile money subscribers in Mozambique.
facts.quote: As of 2016, there were about three million mobile money subscribers in Mozambique.

facts.fact: Five out of ten mobile phone users in Mozambique use mobile money.
facts.quote: The Survey shows that five out of ten mobile phone users use mobile money in Mozambique

facts.fact: 63 percent of urban mobile phone users use mobile money, compared with 29 percent of rural users.
facts.quote: 63 percent of mobile phone users in urban areas use mobile money and only 29 percent in rural areas.

facts.fact: About 60 percent of Mozambicans aged 15 and older do not have mobile phones.
facts.quote: A significant proportion of Mozambicans (15 years and older) do not have mobile phones (60%).

facts.fact: Among 49 African countries, Research ICT Africa ranks Mozambique third on 1GB data pricing, ahead of Ghana, Kenya and South Africa.
facts.quote: Among 49 African countries, Research ICT Africa ranks Mozambique third above Ghana, Kenya and South Africa.

facts.fact: The After Access survey forming part of this research covers 20 countries in the Global South, 10 of them in Africa.
facts.quote: forms part of a survey of 20 countries in the Global South (10 in Africa)
